sub: You let the model pick its own training data. Where does it end up?
foot: the two handles  ·  a round-one forecast  ·  two interventions  ·  the limits
narration: You have a model that writes answers. Instead of paying people to rank them, you let the model pick which of its own answers to train on. Run that loop a few rounds and what comes out is not the model you started with, and nothing in your evaluation suite told you which way it would move. Loops like this run in production. So which parts of one can you reach, and can you tell in round one where it ends up.

caption: One round: six candidates per prompt, a judge keeps two, train on those two, re-measure
narration: Each round the model writes six candidates per prompt, a judge keeps two, the model is fine-tuned on those two, then held-out prompts re-measure its value, zero to one. For the gambling organism, the share of answers picking the risky gamble. For the insecure-code organism, how insecure its answers to three fixed questions about its coding habits read, scored by its frozen base model.

caption: Spread, agreement, and the gap they predict: the kept mean minus the pool mean
narration: Two numbers come out of every round. Spread is the standard deviation of the candidates' value scores. Agreement is the correlation between the judge's preferences and those scores. Both are measured inside each prompt's pool and averaged over prompts.

kicker: WHY THOSE TWO AND NOT OTHERS
headline: Spread times agreement is the gap, and training moves the value there
sub: gap reconstructed at R² 0.80 over 367 rounds  ·  next value at MAE 0.081 over 340 rounds, against 0.128
narration: Their product reconstructs the round's kept mean minus pool mean at R squared zero point eight zero over three hundred sixty-seven rounds, nothing fitted. Training then moves the value to that kept mean, predicting the next value at mean absolute error zero point zero eight one over three hundred forty rounds, against zero point one two eight for no change, every condition held out.

caption: 32 self-only four-round runs by round-one agreement and spread; on this subset endpoint MAE 0.159 against 0.269
narration: Chain the two steps and you can forecast instead of react. Read spread, agreement, and pool composition in round one, then iterate with those held fixed. Final values land at mean absolute error zero point one one eight, against zero point four three one for no change.

caption: Two interventions on loops that were already running
narration: Both handles are reachable. One insecure-code run had gone flat, every candidate scoring the same, leaving the judge nothing to choose between. I mixed in base model answers, spread returned, and the stuck value eroded. A run near the top of the scale reversed when a min-risk oracle judge put agreement at minus one.

kicker: WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY YOU
headline: A band is a range, not a number, and agreement drifts
sub: 89% of observed endpoints inside the 80% band  ·  two model families  ·  small models  ·  short runs  ·  filtered SFT
narration: What this does not buy you. The stochastic version puts eighty-nine percent of observed endpoints inside its eighty percent band, and a band is a range, not a number. Agreement also drifts mid run, because it depends on the candidate distribution in front of the judge, which training keeps changing.

kicker: WHAT WOULD HAVE TO HOLD BEFORE ANYONE LEANED ON THIS
checks: more model families, larger models, longer runs
DPO, online RL against a learned reward model, constitutional feedback
moral judgment, AI identity, emergent misalignment
closer: Which artificial selection mechanisms can be engineered into virtuous cycles?
narration: Before anyone leans on this, three things have to hold. More model families, larger models, longer runs. Update rules other than filtered supervised fine-tuning. Values wider than risk preference and insecure-code self-description. As A I takes over more of its own post-training, whether a loop reinforces restraint or amplifies reward hacking has to be readable in round one.
